title: Divide by 1 to 15
subtitle: Times tables to 15, backwards
bounds: PROTOCOL 4c, facts range cartridge. Forms: R is p ÷ a = ? (answer the quotient), C is p ÷ ? = b (answer the divisor), S is ? ÷ a = b (answer the dividend); p = a × b, the times table read backwards, never ÷ 0, no 0 ÷ ? = 0. Divisors and quotients 0-15, the 11-15 rows are the point. T1 R: easy rows to 15, at least 12 with an 11-15. T2 R: 11-15 with 3 or 4 (at least 12). T3 R: 11-15 with 6-9 or 11-15 pairs (at least 12). T4 C: 3-15 facts with an 11-15 (at least 12). T5 S: 3-15 facts with an 11-15 (at least 8), any 3-15 fact (at least 4), plus C (4 with an 11-15). Wrong choices: distinct non-negative integers up to 999, at least 2 near and at most 1 far. R: near within 2 of the quotient (GROUP_OFF q+-1, +-2), far SUBTRACTED p-a, MULTIPLIED p×a, TENS_SLIP q+-10. C: near within 2 of the divisor (MISSING_ONE_OFF a+-1, ARITH +-2), far MISSING_SUBTRACTED p-b, MISSING_MULTIPLIED p×b. S: near within the larger factor of the dividend (START_GROUP_OFF p+-a, START_ADDED a+b, START_TENS p+-10 when a factor is 11 or more, with a twin ones digit when p is 20 or more). The answer's rank among the four values is spread 15-35% per tier.

tiers.name: Easy rows to 15
tiers.description: Divide by the easy rows, teens included.

tiers.name: Teens and 3s, 4s
tiers.description: Divide the teens by 3s and 4s. Split into tens and ones.

tiers.name: Teens and 6 to 15
tiers.description: Divide the teens by 6 and up. Split into tens and ones.

tiers.name: Missing divisors
tiers.description: Find the divisor: 135 ÷ ? = 9. Think 9 times what.

GROUP_OFF.student: Close: a group or two off. Multiply your answer by the divisor to check.
GROUP_OFF.teacher: Quotient off by one or two: counted a group or two too many or too few.

SUBTRACTED.student: Divide, don't subtract. Ask how many of the divisor fit in the dividend.
SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts the divisor from the dividend (p − a) instead of dividing.

MULTIPLIED.student: Divide, don't multiply. Ask how many of the divisor fit in the dividend.
MULTIPLIED.teacher: Multiplies dividend and divisor (p × a) instead of dividing.

TENS_SLIP.student: Right ones digit, wrong tens. Multiply back to check the size.
TENS_SLIP.teacher: Quotient off by ten: right ones digit, tens place slipped.

MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: One off. Try your number in the problem: does the division work out?
MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Missing divisor off by one: stopped a fact early or late in the table.

MISSING_SUBTRACTED.student: Don't subtract. Ask: what times the answer shown makes the dividend?
MISSING_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts (p − b) to find the missing divisor instead of asking what times b makes p.

MISSING_MULTIPLIED.student: Too big. Divide the dividend by your number: is it the answer shown?
MISSING_MULTIPLIED.teacher: Multiplies (p × b) to find the missing divisor instead of dividing or asking what times b makes p.

START_GROUP_OFF.student: One group off. Multiply the two numbers you see, no more, no less.
START_GROUP_OFF.teacher: Missing dividend off by one divisor (a × (b +- 1)): counted one group too many or too few.

START_ADDED.student: Don't add. To undo dividing, multiply the two numbers you see.
START_ADDED.teacher: Adds the divisor and quotient (a + b) to find the missing dividend instead of multiplying back.

START_TENS.student: Right ones digit, wrong tens. Multiply the two numbers, then check the size.
START_TENS.teacher: Missing dividend off by ten: right ones digit, tens place slipped.

items.explanation: 0 ÷ 12 = 0: zero shared into groups of 12 leaves none, and 12 × 0 = 0.
0 ÷ 10 = 0: zero shared into groups of 10 leaves none, and 10 × 0 = 0.
15 ÷ 15 = 1: any number divided by itself is 1.
0 ÷ 8 = 0: zero shared into groups of 8 leaves none, and 8 × 0 = 0.
0 ÷ 2 = 0: zero shared into groups of 2 leaves none, and 2 × 0 = 0.
12 ÷ 12 = 1: any number divided by itself is 1.
28 ÷ 7 = 4 because 7 × 4 = 28. Neighbour fact: 7 × 3 = 21, plus one more 7.
32 ÷ 8 = 4 because 8 × 4 = 32. Neighbour fact: 8 × 3 = 24, plus one more 8.
24 ÷ 8 = 3 because 8 × 3 = 24. Neighbour fact: 8 × 2 = 16, plus one more 8.
18 ÷ 3 = 6 because 3 × 6 = 18. Neighbour fact: 3 × 5 = 15, plus one more 3.
54 ÷ 6 = 9 because 6 × 9 = 54. Neighbour fact: 6 × 8 = 48, plus one more 6.
12 ÷ 4 = 3 because 4 × 3 = 12. Neighbour fact: 4 × 2 = 8, plus one more 4.
21 ÷ 7 = 3 because 7 × 3 = 21. Neighbour fact: 7 × 2 = 14, plus one more 7.
32 ÷ 4 = 8 because 4 × 8 = 32. Neighbour fact: 4 × 7 = 28, plus one more 4.
63 ÷ 7 = 9 because 7 × 9 = 63. Neighbour fact: 7 × 8 = 56, plus one more 7.
21 ÷ 7 = 3 because 7 × 3 = 21. Neighbour fact: 7 × 2 = 14, plus one more 7.
28 ÷ 7 = 4 because 7 × 4 = 28. Neighbour fact: 7 × 3 = 21, plus one more 7.
81 ÷ ? = 9: 9 × 9 = 81, so ? = 9. A square fact: 9 times itself makes 81.
225 ÷ ? = 15: 15 × 15 = 225, so ? = 15. A square fact: 15 times itself makes 225.
